title: Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters
main_claim: Assume the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition of the companion paper (Thm 1.1 of Parent). Then for a split semisimple G over a global function field at full level D, every occurring cuspidal excursion parameter sigma_nu has a global Arthur enhancement. That means an algebraic phi_nu: SL2 -> L with raising element in O_nu and a continuous pure tau_nu: W_U -> Z_L(phi_nu(SL2)) with reductive closure, such that sigma_nu(w) = tau_nu(w) phi_nu(diag(a^deg w, a^-deg w)) on the whole Weil group.

issues.location: Theorem 1.1 / Theorem 1.2 (manuscript.tex, Sec 1); all of Sec 2-7
issues.description: The main theorem is conditional on the companion paper's Theorem 1.1, and it also relies on that paper's Sections 2-3 and Lemma 6.4 (enhanced Satake, path rotation, central sheaves, constituent purity). This dependence is stated openly. It is not circular, because the companion paper does not use this one, but the result is only as strong as the companion paper. The sibling audit of the companion paper (rank 83) found no gap.

issues.description: Not a demonstrated error. This is a coverage limit. The fully faithful coherent and Koszul realization of the Iwahori trace, the identification End(P)^op = affine Hecke algebra pulled back to the slice, and the spherical retract B = O_Y are long categorical arguments. I did not verify them line by line, and both halves of the final contradiction (the vanishing of q_Pi^*f and its survival) depend on them.
issues.evidence: Theorem~\ref{thm:local-test-model}: "The ordinary $H$-equivariant algebra $\End(P)^{\rm op}$ is the affine Hecke algebra with parameter $r$, pulled back along the etale map on its center."

coverage: Read Sec 1 (statement), all of Sec 2 (cohomological inputs, matrix-entry action, degree-two operation and the relation Ad(b(w))e = q^deg e, framed modules, finite type of R), and all of Sec 3: the choice of test places (connectedness of centralizers via Weyl stabilizers), the open resonance orbit, the BMR tuple-conjugacy lemma, the open-orbit enhancement criterion (Jacobson-Morozov parabolic containment, Levi projection, complete-reducibility projection, lifting through the finite center), the purity norm/orthogonality argument, and the boundary corollary. Also read the Sec 5 slice lemma, the equation-scheme dimension count (Y is a complete intersection of dim H) and the flag-slice lemma; the Sec 6 nearby-cycles setup, constituent inclusion, weight bound, the sign of the simultaneous lower bound (checked against e-classes in degree 2 with m-weight -2, which gives sheared degree 0) and the Ind/QCoh comparison (Postnikov filtration of Li^*i_*Q); and all of Sec 7. In Sec 7 I verified the bad-flag lemma, including c_Delta = Tr(ad m ad delta) = Tr((ad delta)^2) > 0 using B(h,delta) = 0 and the lexicographic Borel ordering (-delta, m, eps). I also checked the fiber-zero splitting, the noetherian-induction proof of successive tensor vanishing, the adjunction to R_n, the simple-quotient argument that bad idempotents act by zero (End(B) = O(U_H)^H is independent of e, and the composite vanishes at (1, open-orbit e)), and the H^0 cone-quotient computation. Sec 4 (enhanced Frobenius-compatible Iwahori category) and most of Sec 5 (trace transfer, Koszul duality, spherical reconstruction) were only skimmed and taken on trust.
